I've been using a much fancier (and more expensive) "computer stand" for a couple of years, but it finally bit the dust (the weld that holds the desktop onto the central support column failed). So I started the search for a replacement, one that maybe wasn't so fancy but would last longer.

Of course I came to Amazon -- they have everything! -- and found a number of options. This looked like the best fit, so I ordered it.

I'm absolutely thrilled with it. Seriously, it's even better than I expected, even with my experience with Lifetime tables (which has been excellent). This little table is the PERFECT size for my laptop, a mug of coffee, and a couple of other items (reading glasses, etc.). It's lightweight enough that I can easily scoot it out of the way when I need to move around (get a coffee refill, etc.). My only quibble is that I wish it came in black, but that's absolutely NOT a deal breaker.

This feels far more stable than my old computer stand even when it was new, and it's not likely to have any similar problems. I love that I can adjust the height, too.

Overall, this is a solid 5-star item. Would happily purchase again if the need arises.

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise) This is the second case I have gotten that I could not give a good rating because of the bottom part, which does not fit with the adapter (to allow older devices to work with the new iPhone), and it does not fit most professional cables that go into the headphone jack.
Because my car has a built-in charger and system that plays with i-technology (previous generations), I HAVE to use the adapter, not just the new wire. Because I am a dancer and instructor and use my phone for job every day, I HAVE to have a case that lets me plug into our system. For those reasons, this case, like the last one I got, is useless to me.

Could you peel back the case to leave the bottom exposed? Yes. But over time, this warps the plastic and creates a loose fit, and putting it on and taking if off can cause the screen protector to come off around the edges.

Could you cut part of the bottom to allow the adapter and wires to fit? No. The plastic is thick enough that the wire will still not fit the headphone jack. As for the adapter, it might fit, but it will want to come out because the thickness, again, will make it want to separate.

So far, the only case to fit my iPhone is a pretty cheap import that has very thin plastic and is generally not a great case either. Is it a design problem with the phone as well? Maybe, but the people making cases should take that into account and design something that works with the iPhone 5 as it is, not as we wish it were. I guess I'm keeping my brand X case a bit longer.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise)

text_fidelity_a: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop First let me say that I grew up typing on actual typewriters and I find myself getting really nostalgic about those days the older I get.  Not that I mind sleek, modern keyboards.  I do a great deal of writing, so I have adapted to the various styles as they've come out.  This particular keyboard is nice and pleasant to work on, but I wouldn't say it's a true typewriter style experience.  The keys are too flat and too round for that.  If you are like me and you do a lot of typing and can adapt yourself quickly between different keyboards you will probably enjoy this one.  I do find myself making a lot of typos that I normally wouldn't when I'm working on it though.  The mouse is honestly just annoying.  There is no actual switch to turn it off, just a button right on top that seems to 'wake' it when it goes dormant, so if you're prone to bumping it around or accidentally dropping things on it or if you plan on using it in multiple places for any reason whatsoever you will find yourself getting frustrated with just how easy it is to turn it back on.  The scroll wheel is fantastic, but the one on my previous mouse no longer works at all, so that might be the reason why I like it so much.  The accuracy of its tracking leaves a lot to be desired and it's quite loud when you click it, but I do tend to prefer to keep my environment quiet.  All in all I would not purchase this again both because the keyboard design is just 'off' in enough nit-picky ways to make it frustrating (so many typos) and because the mouse tracking and lack of a true 'off' switch makes it frustrating to actually use it.  Both the keyboard and the mouse are really pretty to look at and well built for what they are, but I wouldn't call them truly functional even though they do work.  If you're just doing minor browsing and not a lot of typing they would be fine for that, but if you're someone that does a lot of writing or anything that requires precision tracking of the mouse like playing games or working in paint programs you should probably skip this set.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop

text_fidelity_a:
Sony DCR-SX45 Handycam Camcorder (Blue) The camcorder was bought to record some interviews and later to be used for general videos. It worked very well for the interviews with excellent image quality and color balance. The audio was good but not great with the built-in microphone, something that I expected.

I have tried to use it for other general videos with a fair number of action shots of animals, planes and other moving targets. I find the screen to be difficult to see in direct sunlight, one of the main reasons I strongly prefer an optical viewfinder over a screen. The audio is okay, and the video quality is very good in bright and moderate light. In very low light, it starts to suffer as most camcorders in this price range do until it eventually becomes almost unusable.

I am not enamored with the controls. I find that they do not fall where I need them. The still camera is only okay, though it does give a 12 MP image. Get a DSLR or quality P&S if you are serious about still images.

If you want a very good, moderate cost camcorder for moderate to bright lighting and can live with the controls, this is a good choice.
text_fidelity_b: Sony DCR-SX45 Handycam Camcorder (Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
Macbook Pro Charger 96W Usb-C Power Adapter For Macbook Pro Air 13 14 15 16 Inch Mac Book Retina M2 M1 2022 2021 2020 2019 2018 2017 2016 Usb-C To C Fast Charging Charger For IPad Pro/All USB C Device My laptop came with a Dell PA1900-02D (9T215) which I still have and works fine. I wanted a second charger for another location. The EasyStyle SK90B195462looks like the original but is much lighter, probably due to being a switching power supply. My laptop had been discharged down to 5% prior to plugging the replacement charger in. The connector fit fine, but the laptop did not recognize the charger and warned that it may not work. I figured that's just Dell telling me it's not a Dell accessory. I permanently shut off the warning (an option) and continued to use the EasyStyle charger. Charging appeared normal and battery status was indicated as charging. However, after a short while it seemed stuck at 11% charge. I came back a few hours later and it was still indicating at 11%. I plugged in the Dell charger and 100% full charge was indicated immediately. I unplugged the Dell charger and the computer still indicated nearly full charge. I plugged in the new EasyStyle charger and the indication was charging and still near full charge.
My conclusion is that the charger works, but may cause the computer to give incorrect charge status under some conditions and it will be best to unplug the charger to get an accurate battery status.
text_fidelity_b: Macbook Pro Charger 96W Usb-C Power Adapter For Macbook Pro Air 13 14 15 16 Inch Mac Book Retina M2 M1 2022 2021 2020 2019 2018 2017 2016 Usb-C To C Fast Charging Charger For IPad Pro/All USB C Device

Philips SHE9850 in-Ear Headphones with Advanced Acoustics (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Some people prefer their headphones outside of their ears, with comfortable ear cushions and other features, such as the [[ASIN:B00007056H Koss KTXPRO1 Titanium Portable Headphones with Volume Control]]. Others prefer wearing their headphones in the privacy of their own ears, with the added bonus of noise isolation.

There are good reasons for choosing either type depending on your personal preferences, such as comfort levels, where and when you're using them, what you're listening to, and whether or not you have to share with other people.

For general use at home, I use the regular "outie", especially for movies or music with inappropriate language that I'd rather not play in surround sound in the presence of young `uns. I also let my son use it when I'd rather not hear another note from the Jonas Brothers. However, in the wee hours of the morning when the only creature stirring is me, I prefer to use in-ear headphones, which shut out everything except the music.

At work, I hardly ever use headphones due to the telephone ringing off the hook, but at lunchtime I sometimes use the in-ear headphones for peace and quiet. I drive to work, so no headphones are needed for the daily commute.

This is a fairly expensive model, but it's worth every cent if you can safely use headphones that cut out most external noise.

Pros:

1. Really nice packaging, easy to open, simple instruction manual
2. Cool, sleek and compact black metal carrying case included, with a cleaning tool and cable clip as accessories.
3. It comes with three different sizes of rubber caps, and as Goldilocks might say, one is for ears that are big, one's for smaller ears, and one will no doubt be just right. Changing caps is simple too.
4. It also includes a pair of memory foam sleeves that fit so snugly in your ears that you may think they belong there.
5. The caps are washable, once you dry them properly before using them again.
6. The sound is marvelous, clear and true, and there's no need to raise the volume to sonic boom levels.
7. The headphones are clearly marked left and right, and are at an angle for easy insertion and a tight seal
8. Drastically cuts down on external noise

Cons:

1. Unless you're using it for an IPod or other portable device, the cord is too short.
2. May feel a bit weird for some people due to the superior noise isolation.
3. You may experience "ewwwwwwwwwww" moments when your friends grab them and try them on. These aren't for sharing.
4. Try saying "in-ear headphones" out loud six times

If you're looking for an excellent pair of (deep breath) in-ear headphones, I think you'll be pleased with this one.

Amanda Richards, July 2, 2008
text_fidelity_b: Philips SHE9850 in-Ear Headphones with Advanced Acoustics (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

To securely close the cover, there is a flap that has 2 snaps. You wrap the cover around the back of the camera, and snap the flap closed with the 2 snaps. I'm not a fan of snaps. These were easy to snap closed, but Velcro would have been much easier.
There is a strap attached to the inside of the cover. It came with 2 ways of attaching the cover to your camera so you don't lose the cover:
1. a piece of leather that attaches to the camera by screwing it into the tripod mount. This piece attaches to the strap with a snap. I could see either end of the leather coming apart - the side with screw could detach or the snap could release.
2. A ring that can go around the lens. This ring attaches to the strap with a snap. I don't like having things attached to my lens and the snap could release.
I came up with my own method of securing the cover to my camera. The bottom of my battery grip has a connection point for a strap. I had an extra set of Op Tech Uni Loop connectors (https://www.amazon.com/OP-TECH-USA-1301062-Uni-Loop/dp/B0010HA6A6/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1485137755&sr=8-1&keywords=optech+uni+loop).
I attached one end to the bottom of the battery grip. I attached the other connector to the strap by looping the strap thru the connector loop and snapping the two snaps on the strap together. Using the uni loop connectors, I clicked the two pieces together. I think the weakest point is where the snaps are attached. I'm going to sew a few stitches next to the strap as a precaution in case the snaps come undone. You can use any type of strap to secure the cover to the camera. I also attached a photo using an extra camera strap from one of my point and shoot cameras. If I used this method, I would still sew a few stitches next to the snap. I like the uni loop method. If the cover gets in the way, I can just disconnect the uni loop clips.
I'm happy with this cover even though I'm using a different method of attaching the cover to my camera. I dropped the rating to a 4 because of the use of the snaps.
text_fidelity_b: OP/TECH USA Soft Pouch Digital D-Pro (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Elgood Tabletop Vacuum Cleaner with Cleaning Brush,Eraser dust Vacuum USB Charging,Best Desk Vacuum No Dead Angle Cleaning(Green) Like many single guys I have various pockets of dust scattered around my place. My desk, behind the computer towers and monitors where all the cords are piled up is one of the worst. So a handheld vacuum to clean all those nooks and crannies sounded like a good idea. Sadly, this is not the portable vacuum that I am looking for.

A few design flaws were obvious as soon as I took this out of the box and started charging it. There is no stand or holder for the vacuum so it has to sit directly on the brushes you've just been cleaning with. The light indicating when the vacuum is charging/fully charged is pinhole size, barely visible from any distance. So I had to go pick it up and squint at the light to see if it was charged up. The little brush for cleaning the inside of the vacuum is one more tiny thing to keep track of and is easily lost.

Even more flaws became obvious as soon as I tried to use the vacuum. With the nozzle on I tried to clean the back of my desk where all the computer wires are. The nozzle immediately jammed up on hair and dust balls. That area is still as dusty now as it was before I tried to vacuum it. Next I tried cleaning some flat surfaces. The brushes pushed the dust back and forth while barely vacuuming any of it up. I put my hand across the bottom of the brushes and could not feel any suction at all. When I put my finger right into the center hole that the dust was supposed to be scooped up into, I could barely feel a tiny amount of suction. I still very much like the idea of a handheld vacuum but I very much do not like this one and cannot recommend it to anyone.
text_fidelity_b: Elgood Tabletop Vacuum Cleaner with Cleaning Brush,Eraser dust Vacuum USB Charging,Best Desk Vacuum No Dead Angle Cleaning(Green)

text_fidelity_a:
Eton - American Red Cross ZoneGuard Weather Radio, White, Siren/Buzzer (90dB), 3 Color LED Alert Light Bar, LCD Display, Detachable Stand, AC Power Adapter, AA Battery Operated I like the basic design of this -- the small sleek size, nice layout of buttons, large display. The radio reception seems to be decent, although mounting it on the wall is not possible in my area, since I have to turn it various directions to get a couple of local AM stations. Weather band reception is OK, as is FM reception.

That's about where my positive feelings for this little radio end.

It is way too difficult to set up, NOT with regard to the physical aspects of hitting the correct buttons in the correct sequence, but rather in terms of deciphering and understanding the instructions. The instruction leaflet, such as it is, is written in such small type that it's nearly impossible to read. I finally went to the Eton website and downloaded the instruction manual there, then "zoom"ed it so I could read how to set the time, store radio stations, etc.

Then there's the issue of the S.A.M.E. codes. I had never heard of this technology before I got this radio. NO WHERE in the included instructions is there any mention of NOAA, or even the "S.A.M.E." designation. On the Amazon product page, there is a mention of "S.A.M.E." in one of the product features bullets, and "NOAA" in another product feature bullet on the product page here on Amazon, but nothing that explains what "S.A.M.E. codes" actually ARE. The instruction manual tells you how to "Select the county" -- OK, so what does THAT mean? The instructions don't tell you that "Select the county" really means "enter the NOAA S.A.M.E. codes." You're not "selecting" anything; you need to know the S.A.M.E. code(s) for the desired area(s), and then ENTER those according to the instructions.

This was my first weather radio -- and I'm generally fairly good at figuring things out -- but this had me confused for a good 15-20 minutes while I searched via google for "county code," "weather county code," etc. Finally found the NOAA site and the codes, and entered the one for my county.

And I STILL don't know what "Setting Defeat" means. I mean, I know how to set it, and I can read what the manual says, but it doesn't really tell me WHY I might want to enable or disable "defeat," and what, precisely, it enables or disables ("ENABLE: Alert when receiving a message. DISABLE: Displays the message on the LCD when receiving a message" -- does that mean that when it's enabled, you DON'T get a message displayed on the LCD when receiving a message? What kind of Alert happens when it's enabled? the flashing light? the siren? what, precisely, am I "defeating" with this??)

I have no idea if the weather alert part of the radio works. We've had one National Weather Service-issued high wind warning here in the Pacific NW since I received and programmed the radio, and it didn't set off the alert -- no light flashing, no "message," nothing. I intend to take this along on an extended road trip this summer (reprogramming the S.A.M.E. codes along the route), and I figure I'll probably encounter some sort of "alert-able" weather event along the way. I'll update this review then if that part works.

Meanwhile, I'm giving this 2 stars -- it works pretty well as a compact "clock radio," doesn't take up a lot of space, and has decent reception. But Eton REALLY needs to do something about the instructions. The ones included with the product are useless, and the copy on the website isn't much better.
text_fidelity_b: Eton - American Red Cross ZoneGuard Weather Radio, White, Siren/Buzzer (90dB), 3 Color LED Alert Light Bar, LCD Display, Detachable Stand, AC Power Adapter, AA Battery Operated

System is much more responsive now and this product fit the bill. Comes in a 2 pack (one for each end), not expensive, easy to install, and comes with both the wall insert and a trim cover plate. Apple Watch 42mm Space Gray Aluminum Black Sport Band I recently purchased two original gen watches. Did not buy them on Amazon as I was looking specific bands. This review is of the Watch, not the seller.

Awesome technology. After reading a Consumer Reports Oct 2016 online review of the first gen watch, I bought one for my wife and one for myself. We wanted the stainless case with sapphire lens. We previously purchased both a series 2 aluminum and series 1 aluminum and returned both. Really wanted the stainless sapphire combo without spending a lot. We considered these nice toys. We both have Rolexes and the sapphire lens is virtually indestructible. Our Rolexes went into the jewelry box as these Apple smart watches are both useful and enjoyable.

These are not toys. Extremely useful watches. Great features. Use Siri to make calls off your contact list. You don't have to type the number on a tiny screen. On the walking track, or while walking the dog, glance at your watch if a call or text comes in. Don't have to fumble with the phone while holding a leash. Have the music icon on the Watch face. It allows me to activate and change songs or albums without pulling my watch out. Have the calendar on my watch face. Quick glance each morning keeps me from forgetting about appointments. Weather icon also on my face. Tap it twice and it goes from current temp to 10 day forecast. Activity monitor on face lets me track my steps without having to pull my phone out.

All in all, an extremely useful item.

Disregard all early reviews. The updates make the original gen watch an extremely useful item. And a fun toy to boot.

LeadsaiL Wireless Computer Mouse, 2.4G Portable Slim Cordless Mouse Less Noise for Laptop Optical Mouse with 4 Buttons, AA Battery Used, USB Mouse for Laptop, Desktop, MacBook Great shape, very much like the classic and ubiquitous Logitech. I like that the pairing device is on-board. Lightweight and simple, a mouse is important for me if needing to get serious work done, especially anything with CAD or Visio.

The big question you need to ask yourself is, do you want a Bluetooth version or one like this that has its own receiver. It seems to me that if you always use this with the same computer and you have Bluetooth built in to the computer, then you probably want Bluetooth. Conversely, if you want this to use with multiple computers and/or you don't have Bluetooth built in to any one of the computers you will use the mouse with, then you'd want something like this. Apple 80 GB iPod AAC/MP3 Video Player 5.5 Generation (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I got one of these for the holidays last year (12/06) and I was totally stoked. This was my first iPod--what a shame that it turned out to be such a fragile, poorly engineered device. I mean, this thing got dropped once from about 2.5 feet (it was only 2 months old) and it was TOAST (and it was in a plastic hardshell case!). I have had Laptops that survived worse. Come to think of it, I've had a lot of (far cheaper) devices that are better able to take abuse than this $400 item--including TV remotes, cell phones, Nintendo Game Boys (designed to be nearly indestructible), OTHER MP3 PLAYERS, etc. It seems that a physically appealing design does not necessarily equate to superior engineering--quite the opposite in this case. I do like it, and the replacement I got from Apple works very well. It's great looking and it does the job well. Too bad I'm so terrified of dropping it that I had to buy a big, bulky silicone case to improve its chances of survival. Let me tell ya, in its crash-test-dummy outfit, it no longer looks even the slightest bit sleek.

Have you ever dropped your keys when getting out of the car? Your cell phone? If you answered yes to either of the above, then you can probably expect to drop your iPod one day. I hope you have a (thickly) carpeted garage--or that it lands on your foot. Bottom line: If I were thinking of getting an MP3 player, iPod or another brand, it would have zero moving parts; on other words, I would buy a flash-based device instead of one with a hard drive.

I also cannot help but wonder why Nintendo does not take what they have learned about building child-proof, nearly indestructible portable gaming devices and apply this to a worthy competitor to the iPod. I would be the first in line...

I gave this product 3 stars because it does a good job of what it is touted to do: play MP3s & video/images. In fact, the user interface, including the GUI and the click wheel is one of the nicest, most intuitive designs I have ever seen on a piece of consumer electronics equipment. Too bad it's put together so cheaply. Grossly overpriced? Most definitely. I hope the iPhone turns out to be a higher quality piece.

---

UPDATE: 8/2013: still working fine... :)
text_fidelity_b: Apple 80 GB iPod AAC/MP3 Video Player 5.5 Generation (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a: Linksys LGS308MP Business Poe+ Smart 8 Port Gigabit Network Switch (130W),Black Pretty much a plug and play device; 1 minute to install.  There is supposed to be a configuration program that you can access, but I wasn't able to do so with the IP address given in the instructions.  It wasn't necessary anyway, as the device functions just fine on a simple network without any additional configuration.  There are two things I didn't like about it compared to my old switch, that I was replacing.  First of all, it is a bit larger than my old switch at 8 1/2 inches long compared to my old one that is only 6 1/2 inches.  Also, the power supply is considerably larger at 6 inches long and 3 inches wide and 1 inch thick.  My old switch uses only a large plug that is 1 3/4 x 1 3/4 x 1 1/4.  The second thing I didn't like is that there are no indicator lights to show the functioning ports.  My old switch has lights for each port that is working, which is nice.  You may prefer not to have any lights and if so, this Linksys switch may be to your liking.  Note: there is a disc included with documentation, but I didn't find it to be of any particular use.  On the plus side, this does appear to be a quality, heavy duty switch, so might be well suited for a commercial application (such as in an unattended area, like a computer room in a large business).  It appears to weigh nearly twice what my old switch did, so it is solid.  I have used Linksys products before and found them to be good quality with no issues.  You can buy a cheaper switch that is smaller and does essentially the same thing at a considerably lower price, but you most likely won't get the same quality as you would with this switch.  Also this switch does apparently have a POE (power over internet) feature and if you need that, you also might want to get this.  I don't see a need for POE in my configuration.  Possibly overkill for typical home office, but if you want a good quality switch, it might be worth the extra cost (or not).

Samsung 860 QVO SSD 4TB - 2.5 Inch SATA 3 Internal Solid State Drive with V-NAND Technology (MZ-76Q4T0B/AM), Gray I’ve had this SSD for a few days and I also have a 1TB 970 Evo Plus and 1TB 860 Evo and all of them are great! But they do have their drawbacks too.

This drive does really well with SMALL (under 15Gb) workloads. The speeds are right up there (~500MB/s R/W) with my 860 Evo until it gets to about ~14GB at which point it slows down drastically. This is fine for things like boot, games, apps, and most programs.

However, if you do heavy workloads like video editing, file transfers, etc,. where you are regularly moving large (15GB+) files around this is NOT the drive for you. If you are a “heavy” user I highly recommend the 860 Pro. It can keep up those high R/W speeds without slowing down after ~15GB. It will maintain full speed throughout the duration of whatever you are doing.

With that said this is a great drive for light/moderate workloads (gaming, web browsing, small work files, etc.,) and it is at a price that gives you excellent value and quality for your money.

I also really love the Samsung Magician software. It’s basically the main reason why 3/5 of my drives are Samsung. Samsung is also known for making reliable, high quality products. Yes there is a premium compared to cheaper drives but you’re paying that little bit extra for quality & reliability.

I took off 1 Star on this review though because Samsung doesn’t include any of the cables or mounting screws which just doesn’t make sense to me. C’mon Samsung start adding that stuff! text_fidelity_a:
RCA Digital Amplifier for Indoor Antenna I "Cut the cord" and got rid of my satellite service recently, but did miss watching network TV. Consequently, I bought a Mohu Leaf TV antenna. It works well, but I added this amplifier to see if I could pull in more channels.

Short answer: For me, this amplifier works. It added 10 channels to my lineup. There are several caveats: The effectiveness of this amplifier will vary depending on your location and distance from a major city. (I'm about 60 miles from Denver.) My reception does vary depending on the weather, which can be maddening. On a good day, I can get a total of about 40 channels. Many of these channels (almost half) are religious, Spanish and shopping channels that I don't really watch.

Without the amplifier, I get about 30 channels. I have found that moving my Mohu Leaf around on the wall will improve my reception for certain channels. The important thing is to experiment to see what works for you. Check out the excellent resources online for working with an indoor TV antenna. And think of all the money you are saving!
text_fidelity_b: RCA Digital Amplifier for Indoor Antenna

The problem as many have stated is most commercial WiFi system require you log into a splash page after you connect to their network. This router does not have a way to do that. You can try using one of your devices and then clone the MAC address to the router, but this only works if this router is connected to the network with the Ethernet cable port. Most hotels and hospitals no longer have working Ethernet jacks in rooms. If you try and clone the MAC address on the wireless port it creates a conflict and everything stops working.

So to sum up, it works fine as a cheap travel router, but if you have to deal with a splash page on an WiFi only network, it simply will not work. It can’t be that hard to create one of these with a built in browser for splash pages. Anyone listening????

text_fidelity_a:
co2CREA Hard Case with Sleep Mode Replacement for Apple AirPods Max Headphone (Black Case + Inside Red) This is a smart case - no bra needed.

UPDATE: Wrong, alas. I mean, it’s possible to make this case put your headphones to sleep – at least with the version of this case that I have – but it’s such a precise, finicky, painstaking endeavor that it’s nowhere near worth the effort. I’ve taken to using my case just like everybody else does: with the bra inside.

My guess is that what these third-party case makers need to do is what Apple did with the bra: rather than a couple of dime-sized round magnets, they need to put in long, thin magnets that will connect with the sensors in the earcups no matter where in the case they fall. The bra puts the headphones to sleep every time without fail and without the user having to spend several minutes massaging the headphones into just exactly the perfect position so that they’ll go to sleep, so it can be done; the third-party case manufacturers just haven’t yet figured out how Apple did it.

Anyways: I was dreading this case having an horrendous stench to it, based on several reviews I've read. I'm happy to report that while mine has a smell and it is kind of chemical-y, I find the smell neither strong nor entirely unpleasant. It's pretty mild, strength-wise (and I'm sensitive to such things) and I find the smell has a sort of fresh quality to it, despite its chemical nature. Lucky me, I guess. But this, like the Apple bra, is basically half a case. You need the bra to put the headphones to sleep, and this case to give them adequate protection. Hard to believe in this day and age, but there it is. I guess if Apple included a case with these that did everything necessary they would probably charge an additional $200 for it…

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I bought this as a graduation present for my nephew and, of course, had to try it out for a while just to make sure it was "in proper functioning order." (OK, so I like toys even more than the kids do).

Very nice system! It's a nice improvement from earlier Nuvi's I've used. Love the improved software, especially the full-time next-turn indicator (long a favorite feature of mine on Magellan units). The screen layout is attractive and easy to use, even for those of us with less than perfect eyesight.

While I personally like the Magellan systems better for my own use, I picked this for the nephew for a couple of reasons. First, it has features such as the ability to download Google maps directions. Not something I would use, but a nice feature for those who would use it. Second, it has the ability to display the speed limit. While it won't prevent speeding, at least it's a reminder for a younger driver to keep it slow.

I found the routing engine to be top-notch. Every GPS does that a bit different, but every route I planned on it was plotted out in a logical manner. It's a bit slower to detect off-route conditions and re-route compared with Magellans, but certainly does it at an acceptable speed. Boot up and acquitiion time is very good, as it the overall build quality and form factor.

A good option to pick up is a bean bag mount such as a NavMat. Makes it far easier to hide the GPS without any trace to tip off potential theves.

Most important, it has Garmin support - they are far better than Magellan, and can be used as a resource for someone who is using their first GPS. I was sorry to have to hand it back over the the nephew, but he's thrilled with it!
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Flat black cables run smoothly and nearly invisibly against the black cabinet the router sits on. There's plenty of bandwidth, and the hubs don't have to be noticeable to work.

Negative space for the win.

Haribol USB C Hub, MacBook Pro Adapter USB C Dongle, 6 in 1 USB C to HDMI Multiport Adapter with 1000M Ethernet, 4K USB C to HDMI, 3 USB 3.0 Ports, PD Charging Port for MacBook/Pro and Type C Devices Love the new HUB for the MacBook.. it makes the skinny mini mac have the magical powers it lacks!!
We all know and love the fact, that our MacBook has gotten so light/thin.. SOO thin, it is lacking the extra convenience and creature comforts in the import/exports department!!

Having said that… This is a review from the POV of a mom who is anything But, tech savvy! I know, I cannot be the only one out there so, maybe this well help those who don’t speak tech- and just want to know, you know.. the downlow!!? I was gifted a Mac by my fam. for the purpose to do my ABC’s of life- email, online shopping, bills, movie streaming and travel accessibility.. but, soon after receiving I noticed the lack of charging and multi tasking I could do powered off of my new laptop-

• This allows me to plug in the computer to the wall unit and then, attach the hub without needing a million diff. Wall plugs-
•best of all, I can charge my cell phone- Which when I’m traveling, it always seems to have a little battery!
•I can stream movies by plugging in my Roku/Hulu movie device and love that- especially without TV choices.. this is awesome.
•I can also plug in anyone’s else’s cell phone that has somehow forgotten their wall charger- bc, when we travel.. that is always one of us!!
•lastly- I have a small fan/white noise machine that I can’t sleep without.. and this can be plugged into the hub and run all night- or, until I fall fast asleep- I do turn the device to fan a lot during the day.. and love that it’s 12” away from me and can run as long as I need..
•the adapter cord is appropriately sized in length- it is just long enough be placed flat on the table a few inches away but, next too the computer. Yet, it’s not too much excess cord to become a hot, tangled mess.. (Must have been designed by a mama.. one who thought the practicality all the way through!)
•I love that this Hub is small enough to slip into the sleeve I carry my computer in.. I happen to have a small pocket on the front- and it fits perfectly inside.. making this so easy to find.
•The only issue observed was the Hub itself got a tad warm after hours (6+) of use with 4 items constantly plugged in.. I've only noticed this once-
But, wanted to mention so people are aware of/when using multiple items.. they pay attention so, they don’t damage Hub or worse, their computer device!
So, from laymen’s terms and POV- I’m thrilled to have ordered and acquired this item. It’s abilities and convenience are appreciated every time I use it!

text_fidelity_a:
Aftershokz AS450 Sportz M3 Mobile Bone Conduction Headphones with Microphone (Black) purchased for single sided hearing loss after extensive research for "the best" on the market (at this or near this price point).
perks:
i can hear more clearly out of that ear using this headset. (music, netflix dialogue). if you're not deaf in one ear, this is irrelevant.
Can listen while charging, so no "down time" like some other products.
cons:
headset is uncomfortable in multiple positions. i can not really find a good position, but the least uncomfortable- and interestingly enough, the best sound quality is NOT in manufacture explained position: it's over my head with the pods near my temples or behind my ears.
Sound quality is not good, it's better coming through tinny computer speakers, but using those, i can only hear it well on my good ear. It's louder/better/and more clear (can hear fine details in the music) if you wear a headband or tight hat to press the pods against your head- but again comfort is a factor.
Noise leak is a major factor. If you turn it up to "low-normal" listening volume (cell phone set at half volume, headset set to lowest selectable volume) my housemate can still hear music played at arms reach. do not anticipate that you can wear it around others in a quiet room.

would i buy again? no.
Did I return them due to problems as stated above. Yeah.
text_fidelity_b: Aftershokz AS450 Sportz M3 Mobile Bone Conduction Headphones with Microphone (Black)

The right angle connection reduces the depth of the cable behind my receiver but it still sticks out further than I expected. The connectors clip into the ports pretty well, I have moved the receiver around a bunch since adding the cable & it hasn't pulled out. I ordered the 10' cord & needed all of it for my ceiling mounted television installation.
I have never used optical sound cables before but the receiver I picked up used did not have HDMI. My inexperience with these was readily apparent when I couldn't get the plugs to stay in the sockets on the components. I finally discovered that there are tiny, protective caps over the optical input/output.
The right angle connector doesn't fit quite as close as I imagined but it does make a difference in getting the cable behind my receiver on the shelf. The cable blocks whatever connections are below it but that wasn't an issue for my setup. That said, I don't understand why these connections have to be indexed at all if it is just the light going through the center it shouldn't matter what angle it comes in.

text_fidelity_a:
ARRIS SURFboard SB6141 8x4 DOCSIS 3.0 Cable Modem - Retail Packaging- White Update Jan 2016: After only a few months of use, the modem started acting up. At first, a reboot would cure the problem, but it got progressively worse whereas I needed to reboot it every few hours. It then failed to work at all even though all the indicator lights were indicating it was functioning properly. Swapped it with a different modem and all the problems went away.

Normally I would not down rate an item because of a failure since everything can break. However, if you expect to get warranty support for this, forget it. Arris/Motorola will not stand behind their product at all.

If you're OK with this being disposable when it breaks, go for it. It did work well when it was working. But, if you expect to get warranty support/repair/replacement, go for another brand.

Original review:
So far this has been a champ in terms of performance. I'm using it with Cox, and it replaces another DOCSIS 3.0 modem I had been using for the past four years (a Motorola SB6120). I got it mainly because I was concerned that my old modem would eventually die on me, and wanted to have a backup.

Installation was simple (just a quick call to Cox to give them the MAC id and serial number). Connection speeds have been slightly better than the SB6120 and more consistent. This seems to run no warmer than the SB6120, which is to say it's pretty warm but not hot when operating. The indicator lights are brighter on this model which, for me, is not a problem given where I have the modem located, but could be an issue if you have your modem out in the open -- the lights are beacon-bright in a dark room.

I'm hoping to get the same solid, dependable performance out of this that my SB6120 gave me. I'll update the review should reliability prove to be a problem down the road. But, at present, this is performing perfectly.
text_fidelity_b: ARRIS SURFboard SB6141 8x4 DOCSIS 3.0 Cable Modem - Retail Packaging- White

text_fidelity_a:
REETEC Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Over-Ear - [40 Hrs Playing Time, Soft Protein Earpads] Foldable HiFi Stereo Wireless Headphones with Microphone, Deep Bass Headset for Phone, PC, iPad - Rose Gold I've owned many wireless headphones, so this isn't my first rodeo. I wanted something separate to leave paired with my work computer. Earbuds aren't comfortable for me to wear for long periods of time so over-the-ear style is important. I have to admit, I like these more than I expected to. The ear pads are soft and slow to reclaim their shape like memory foam- this makes them extremely comfortable to wear so I don't mind keeping them on for a good portion of my workday. It also has a rubberized cover for the charging port and 3.5mm jack, which is surprisingly nice to find on a headset in this price range!
The sound quality is about on par with what I expected for this price range- that is, it is very good. Not blow-your-mind-amazing like sets that sell for hundreds, but as good if not better than others in this price range. What I didn't like, however, is the microphone quality. Yes, it has a mic, but I'd like to pretend it doesn't. The mic is on the headset by my ears and doesn't seem to be directed towards my mouth. This makes my voice sound distant and muffled, with ambient background noise sometimes on the same level or louder than my voice is. For calls I'd rather use a different headset, but that's OK. This ends up being used paired with my computer rather than my phone. It is pretty decent at passive noise isolation as well, reducing sound around you naturally. The only things I wish were better are the mic and perhaps a physical on/off switch rather than a button, but honestly this is pretty normal for headphones in this price range so I essentially got exactly what I expected.
EDIT:
I loved these so much, I ended up getting another on in another color for a family member. A great value for wireless headphones.
text_fidelity_b: REETEC Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Over-Ear - [40 Hrs Playing Time, Soft Protein Earpads] Foldable HiFi Stereo Wireless Headphones with Microphone, Deep Bass Headset for Phone, PC, iPad - Rose Gold

text_fidelity_a:
Konnek Stein True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.1 Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Sliding Design Charging Case 500mAh, IPX4 Waterproof, Deep Bass Built-in Mic Call for Business & Sports - Black The KONNEK STEIN True Wireless Earbuds are a decent set of wireless earbuds. The sound quality is good, I’ve been using them with music and streaming shows, and I haven’t been disappointed with the sound quality.

I’m not as pleased with the short battery life, touch controls, and lack of audio cues.

I get about 2-3 hours of playback per charge. It’s rare for me to battery drain earbuds, but with this pair, I hear the low battery chime every time I use them.

The touch controls and lack of audio cues go together. The touch controls are super easy to activate on accident. More than once I’ve taken the earbuds out only to find I hit Play while doing so, and they kept playing music. I also activate random controls when adjusting the earbuds in my ears … and I don’t always know what I’ve done. Did I turn ANC on or off? The audio cues are just beeps, not an announcement like “ANC on/ANC off.”

I like the design of the case. It has a sliding top, so you can actually clean the entire area where the earbuds sit. When you put the earbuds inside the case, a light flashes to show their battery level. The case charges wirelessly or via USB-C. There’s only one LED light on the outside of the case, it’s easy to miss when you’re trying to see if the case is charging or not.
text_fidelity_b: Konnek Stein True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.1 Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Sliding Design Charging Case 500mAh, IPX4 Waterproof, Deep Bass Built-in Mic Call for Business & Sports - Black

Mohu Sky 60 TV Antenna, Outdoor, Amplified, 75 Mile Range, Durable Lightweight, Mount Kit Included, Roof or Attic, 4K-Ready, 30 Foot Detachable Cable, Premium Materials for Performance, MH-110585,Black REVISED to 4 Star review: After using the antenna a week, I re-ran the channel search--which I should have done after installing it. I am able to pick up 38 of the 45 channels within a 60 mile radius of my house. They all come in very clearly. The amplifier wasn't working at all, and we determined that the brick was defective. Plugging it into another USB brick didn't really improve the signal by much, but it at least worked.

All-in-all, I'm glad I bought it. I'm able to clearly receive: 4 PBS stations; 3 CBS stations; 1 each NBC and ABC; plus FOX, CW, and an assortment of crap (TCT, HSN, QVC) networks. Enough to make me happy to leave TWC and in the dust.

UPDATE: 8/2/2016 What I have found is that the signals from channels with transmitters within 10 miles are not being up, while those 12 miles and beyond are coming in clearly. I suspect this is due to my location and not the antenna. Still, the amplifier causes the entire thing to not work, so I don't know what's up with that thing.

This antenna arrived as indicated. However, instead of the nearly 45 channels within a 60 mile radius of my home, I'm only able to get about 15. I installed it on the roof, and the direction did not seem to make a difference. NOTES:

Originally, I hooked this up and leaned it against the back of the TV before I had someone install it. I got no more channels installing it on the roof than I did that way.

The amplifier which comes in the box with this antenna actually made the signal worse--not better, so I disconnected that.

Give the few number of channels that actually come through, on hindsight, I would have bought a much cheaper antenna. It does not pull in channels more than about 20 miles away. Even channels 20 miles away aren't received.

Otherwise, the reception on the channels that do come through is great.

All of this may be because I am in an old, downtown neighborhood, with close houses and lots of trees. Although I installed it in an area of the roof free of trees.
text_fidelity_b: Mohu Sky 60 TV Antenna, Outdoor, Amplified, 75 Mile Range, Durable Lightweight, Mount Kit Included, Roof or Attic, 4K-Ready, 30 Foot Detachable Cable, Premium Materials for Performance, MH-110585,Black

text_fidelity_a:
Cleaning Gel 160G, Dust Cleaning Mud for Car, Car Accessories, Keyboard Printers Cameras PC Tablet Laptop Airpods Case Cleaner EDIT: added pictures.

Not bad, about what I imagined having never used a gel glob like this before (but having wanted to for a long time!).

I have only used it on my keyboard. It is my main reason for acquiring it. I am always grossed out by how my keyboard looks. I sometimes use canned air (but ran out) and disinfectant wipes. I really just wanted to see if I could do better with a cleaning glob. I just wanted to know!

It did a great job with the surface of the keys. They look polished and shiny, and not at all greasy nor grimy. I would say it took more effort to get further down the sides, but I may have been too careful/light with my effort. I think next time I will really pressed into the keys and hopefully I can just work the stuff down the sides easier. Going forward, I would still use canned air to get anything out that is deeper down below the keys. And, still using a disinfectant wipe is a good idea these days. I think I will use this as maintenance rather than for going after a super gross keyboard. I like the scent- it smells fresh and clean. Doesn't linger, but while using it it is rather nice.

The look of it after using it to clean my keyboard really makes me want to hurl. I am not sure how often this can be reused, or if it would be better as a one time project use. I mean, it is meant to be used over and over, just not sure if I want to. Again, I think I like the idea of using it as a maintenance item if I plan to use it over and over. There is a little diagram on the container showing how to check if it needs replacing. It doesn't say much, but I surmise that if it goes from the bright color to a dark color, then it needs to be replaced.

Anyway, I think it is worth the try. It really does grab onto the nasty things and pulls it off/out. This wasn't too pricey, and I think stuff like this could be added on to a themed gift- like a car/truck lovers gift, an office supplies gift, and so on. Who knows.

There is some info on the container (a small clear plastic container with screw on lid, and labeling all around) that I will list here:

Directions say:
-- "Do not rub just press!" as well as, "Use with body hands" (lost in translation? maybe means both hands, or put your body into it?)

--Absorbs dirt and dust in cavities. Ideal for all devices and surfaces

--Keep away from direct sunlight and keep in a dry place. Keep away from children, don't eat it

--Ingredients:
Vegetable gum, Bactericide, Quaternium, fragrance, glycerin.

--Made in China

HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA) I got my first PC in 2003, and had a corded mouse. Looking back, I can BARELY remember the mouse that came with that Gateway PC. In 2004, my mom bought a Dell PC and traded me for my Gateway – don’t judge, she just wanted something to browse the internet and play games on.

Between 2003-2005, I used an awkward racecar shaped mouse, but went back to the more streamlined corded mouse for my desktops.

In 2005, when I got a laptop, I got my first wireless mouse and liked it. It was a Logitech.

By 2010, I got my first HP laptop – and as usual, got a specific mouse for it, again Logitech. The reason? My hand. I don’t have very big hands and hate to “splay” my fingers out trying to grip the mouse. That continued with a backup laptop in 2011 with some college money.

I even got “backup” mice, I just LOVED the Logitech ones.

Last year, 2021, I got another HP laptop for my birthday and yes – a “Logi” mouse (M317 – Amazon code B08L8SRJRR; white with purple/pink side grip, flowers on top). This was a bit smaller than my previous mice. But, I love it.

Thinking this might be a bit better – I got it.

Right off – it is a bit “extra”. I can BARELY grip it to get it to do what I need to do. The “thumb” rest was a good idea, the USB rechargeable feature was nice, programmable buttons – a bit beyond me. This is definitely for someone who needs those features.

As far as “quiet” with regards to the scrolling and clicking – I don’t see the need for the feature. When I’m typing on they keyboard that is noisier than my mouse.

It was response and fast – but not enough to justify a purchase of it.

It connects the same way my “Logi” does – USB dongle. Both mice take ONE (1) AA battery

At the current price of $67.52 – this is a definitely no-go for me.
text_fidelity_b: HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA)

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D810 FX-format Digital SLR Camera Body I have had this camera since July 2015 and I find that this camera to be the most incredible camera I have ever owned. I have owned the D700, D800, D600, D610 and still own the D750.The clarity and dynamic range surpasses all of my previous cameras, including my D750.
However, the D810 is very demanding on lenses. Inferior lenses will provide either inconsistent performance, or just plain horrendous results.
Edit: 11/29/2017: After over two years of regular use I have had no problems with this camera. I have never had to clean my sensor, and I change lenses frequently, as I most often use prime lenses. So, I don’t understand why so many people have the need to frequently to “dust off” or clean their sensor. Nor do I understand why some people complain about the fact that most of the outer shell is made of carbon fiber. For years I worked with advanced composites, and carbon fiber is not just cheap plastic, but is used in many high-tech products for its superior strength and light weight.
I can only speak from my own experience and knowledge.
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D810 FX-format Digital SLR Camera Body

text_fidelity_a: StarTech.com 2 Port USB DVI KVM Switch with DDM Fast Switching Technology and Cables - Dual Port DVI USB KVM Switch - DDM KVM Switch (SV231DVIUDDM) If you remember the old game unit switches that allowed you to use multiple devices on one television set, this is like that, only for two computers sharing one monitor, keyboard, mouse, and other peripherals. The simple switch box connects to your monitor ("console") via the kind of cord with plugs on both ends you currently use to connect your monitor to your computer. (You will need an extra cord like this for the the purpose--not included. If you don't have a spare lying around, you should order one with the unit.) You will need the cords you are currently using for each of the two computers to connect them to the box. There are four USB sockets in the "console" section of the box. You plug your keyboard, mouse, and anything else you want to share between the two computers into those. (By the way, KVM stands for Keyboard, Video,Mouse.) The unit is powered, and offers multiple plug styles for international use. There is a place to plug in speakers and a mike for each computer. This switch has made it possible for me to streamline my office space considerably. Previously, I had two monitors, two keyboards, and two mice. It was very awkward. I kept my old computer because it has Adobe CS4, which is fine for my needs and saves me the $50 a month the Creative Cloud would cost. I have not used it much, though. Firing up the old machine was just too much trouble. This new arrangement allows me to flip a switch and access programs I have not been able to use in a long time.
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com 2 Port USB DVI KVM Switch with DDM Fast Switching Technology and Cables - Dual Port DVI USB KVM Switch - DDM KVM Switch (SV231DVIUDDM)

All-New HD 8 Screen Protector,Tempered Glass Screen Protector Film for All-New HD 8 Tablet with Alexa (7th 2017 Release) [9H Hardness] [Crystal Clear] [Bubble Free] EDIT (August 19, 2017): The seller replaced my original screen protector at no charge, and I was able to install the replacement with almost no visible dust particles. It's essential that you wash AND dust the tablet screen before placing the screen protector. This is a thick glass screen protector that provides maximum scratch protection without interfering with touch screen sensitivity. And it's clear that the seller gives excellent customer service. Rating raised from 3 stars to 5 stars.

This KINDLE FIRE HD 8 TEMPERED GLASS SCREEN PROTECTOR was a perfect fit for my 2017 Kindle Fire HD 8 (with Alexa), and it was very easy to apply. It is a stiff glass sheet with gentle adhesive backing.

Unfortunately, I caught a single dust mote between the screen protector and the tablet screen--and this caused a pea-sized (⅜”) air bubble that was highly noticeable. The air bubble was impossible to remove, because the offending dust particle was trapped in the adhesive. (This happened even though I started with a perfectly clean screen. Removing and replacing the screen protector only resulted in even more trapped dust particles.)

I’ve installed enough screen protectors to know that this was just bad luck, but for me the screen protector was a total loss. I think that I’ll try a wet-application film next time, instead of another glass screen protector.

text_fidelity_a:
MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame I love technology, but I can't navigate new tech as easily as I used to. I fear that I'm turning into my parents, who needed my help with programming the VCR. These days, everything seems to have software that you must navigate, and it is seldom as intuitive as it once was for me.

This frame was easy to figure out, though, at least for the features I care about. I skipped right over the parts where it wanted to connect to my network and so forth. I just wanted to upload photos from a micro-SD card, and then have it play them back to me. And it does that very well.

It has a light sensor that adjusts the brightness of the screen automatically if you enable it to, which is a very nice feature that is lacking on my other digital picture frames. I was also able to program it to go to sleep when I'm never up, to save on energy. I didn't want it to be motion activated, as I want it to be displaying photos the moment I walk into the room. Fortunately, this feature is already off by default.

The frame looks really nice, with a small "mat" border around the display. This mat is something that most digital frames are lacking, and let me tell you, this tiny feature makes a huge difference. It really sells the idea that this is a picture frame, instead of merely a digital display. I can't say enough about how much this improves the aesthetic of this frame.

I have a couple of digital frames that I use in a horizontal orientation, so I deleted all my vertical photos from them and moved them onto this one instead, and set it up in a vertical orientation. It is so nice to have the frame matched to the orientation of the photos! You don't get those huge bars on the sides or top/bottom, or if you have it set to crop then you don't crop out 2/3 of the photo!

I have no complaints about this digital photo frame. I can't speak for all of the features, because I have no use for some of them. But the features I wanted work great, and the frame itself looks fantastic!
text_fidelity_b: MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame

I have a few different hubs now because Apple decided I only needed USB-C ports on my laptop. Depending on what I’m doing and how many devices I need to plug in, I’ll either use a hub or adapters.

WiFi signal strength can be impacted by hubs or similar devices, there’s some interference with USB 3.0 and 2.4Ghz networks. It’s a known problem, there’s a lot about it online if you’ve also run into it. I’ve noticed this using other hubs, and I have about the same degree of interference with this one.

I don’t love the design of this hub. I wish the hub’s USB-C plug was straight, not an “L.” While I can still plug in other USB-C things next to the hub, the “L” shape of the plug dictates how the hub sits on my desk.

The hub is bigger than it needs to be. Maybe if the glassy front was repurposed, the USB 3.0 ports laid out in a square rather than a line, it wouldn’t take up as much room on my desk. The big display only has a tiny icon to show me when the hub is on … I just don’t like the wasted space.

text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Speaker,Torteco F60, IPX7 Waterproof Bluetooth Speaker with Loud Stereo Sound,15 Hours Playtime,Gradient Light, Portable Speaker for Home,Outdoor,Travel and Party I try to keep a variety of blue tooth speakers around the house so that any of us can listen to whatever we want as we do things in different areas. Sometimes pod casts are easier if I can move from one room to another, pause the pod cast and then start it up again when relocated in the house.

CHARGING
This speaker has a TYPE C port. I used the same port I use to charge my Samsung TAB S6 and it worked fine.

BLUE TOOTH CONNECTION
This speaker was very fast to hook up with my devices. I had no issues at all with any of my devices.

SOUND
The sound was AMAZING. I had on a recording of someone that used the same recording of the war drumming that I have heard before. When I turned on this speaker to redirect the signal, I almost flew out of my chair. It was really good sound. The sound was divided out nicely too. It was clear and balanced well, depending on the recording of course.

NOISE?
I didn't hear any hissing or other annoying noise with the things I have listened too. It depends on the recording too, of course.

MODES
This goes from Blue Tooth to microSD card to aux-in mode. The first two worked great, but I could not test the Aux, because I dropped my MP3 player and now it wont work - at all.

SONGS/VOLUME
Once in a while I go to increase or decrease volume and end up changing the song, so it is not always fool proof, but most of the time it works well.

LIGHTS
You do not have to run the lights on this. If you choose to, you can have them change in different patterns from very gradual to fast.

TWS SYSTEM
I did not try to set up the TWS system yet because I am not sure what other speaker I have will work with this. For now, I am not able to do it. If that changes, I will try to update.

PHONE
I have only used this once with the phone feature. It seemed to work fine unless walking too far away from the speaker then the person calling could not hear as well.

BATTERY LIFE
I have gotten a lot of use out of this and have not had to recharge the battery yet. There are not any indicators on this which show how much life is left though, and that is one thing I wish it had. I have another speaker with that feature and I prefer that.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This speaker is a great little speaker. It has fantastic sound, good features, and connections worked well.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This speaker is one of my current favorites. It is not tiny, so you have to carry it carefully, but it is really packed with sound and does it well.
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Speaker,Torteco F60, IPX7 Waterproof Bluetooth Speaker with Loud Stereo Sound,15 Hours Playtime,Gradient Light, Portable Speaker for Home,Outdoor,Travel and Party

text_fidelity_a:
JAM XT Extreme Wireless Speaker, Splash Proof, Drop Proof, Dirt Proof IP64 Rating, Carabiner Clip, Built-in Speakerphone, Works with iPhone, Android, Bluetooth Devices, HXP430BK Black I must say this little guy is impressive. For it's size it rocked out in my back porch. Due to the IP64 rating it's a bit heavy but that's a good thing.

I tested this speaker paired with a Sony android phone. Bluetooth pairing was instant. While I didn't quite get a full 30 foot range, I found the actual 27 foot range to be acceptable.

I dropped the speaker from my waist height of 36" onto the concrete pad on my porch. No issues with playability or broken pieces. Although I did notice a slight scuff mark. No biggie.

I like the carabiner feature for hanging the speaker, from a tent ceiling, tree, or post. But I don't see anyone hanging the speaker off a backpack. The weight will cause it to swing wildly. In fact it's heavy enough to be stored in the bottom of your pack.

Recharging was easy, but the rubber plug takes a little finesse to put it back into place.

The sound was crisp with somewhat deep bass undertones. I didn't expect this little speaker to pump out heavy bass, but it's adequate for its size.

I don't recommend that you crank this up too loud when camping in the woods. The loud music might drown out the sounds of an attacking bear or wildebeest.

For the money it's a decent wireless speaker that will survive most outdoor adventures.
text_fidelity_b: JAM XT Extreme Wireless Speaker, Splash Proof, Drop Proof, Dirt Proof IP64 Rating, Carabiner Clip, Built-in Speakerphone, Works with iPhone, Android, Bluetooth Devices, HXP430BK Black

The TV is beside an east wall with large front windows. We had been using one of the flat amplified antennas, and it just couldn't get the distant station. I don't know if the signals didn't want to go through too many walls, or if the high voltage electric transmission line running along the east edge of our front yard was responsible.

When I installed this antenna, I still couldn't get CBS. With the nice long piece of coax attached to it, I experimented with various places. The window was a no go, no matter where it was placed, giving my power line hypothesis some points. Holding it high its full distance to the west worked. We are lucky enough to have a tall bookshelf there, so I stuck it to a metal bookend on top of it. Success!

text_fidelity_a:
Poly - Voyager Focus 2 UC USB-C Headset (Plantronics) - Bluetooth Dual-Ear (Stereo) Headset with Boom Mic - USB-C PC/Mac Compatible - Active Noise Canceling - Works with Teams, Zoom (Certified) & More Ok, so I have to admit at first I was wondering why someone would spend this much on a Bluetooth headset that isn't a feature-rich entertainment one like those from Sony or a major fad brand like Beats, both of which I have some experience with. But this, no... this is actually something different. This is a serious tool for serious use with serious built quality and seriously useful features. Seriously.
For example, the telescoping mouthpiece means you'll get unparalleled mic quality compared to headsets that pick the mic up by your ears (looking at YOU, airpods!), both in clarity and isolation from background noise. You can also physically bend it out of the way, or use the button on the mic itself to mute. Try doing that with airpods. Then there's the button based features. Shortcuts and touch-sensitive buttons are cool on aesthetic devices, but the physical controls on this are an ergonomic user experience DREAM. Everything is easy to access and control, no apps or press-and-hold or counting LED blinks, etc. Sort of makes me miss the old days of phones with physical switches and buttons. When you want your equipment to get serious, this is the sort of user experience you expect. Then there's the charging rack. OMG I love that, I can store it on my desk and it's charging automagically. Pick it up and put it on, ready to go. Never needs to be charged because it's been charging in between uses. Finally, I'm really impressed with the USB dongle option. You see, the one thing I really dislike about wireless headphones is that you usually need to pair it with a device, then unpair it to switch to another device. For example, using my Sony headphones on my phone and tablet, if my wife wants to borrow them for a zoom meeting, I need to pair with her device but then also unpair with mine so that it doesn't keep trying to reconnect to it. Sometimes we just give up and use a wired headset to avoid that mess. Non-bluetooth wireless headsets have a dongle, which makes it easy to swap what you are connected to (no unpairing needed, just move the dongle) but then you can't connect to devices without a USB port like a phone. This is the best of both- you can pair it with your phone, but ALSO use the USB to quickly connect with your desktop or laptop without going through the process of pairing and unpairing. This is the kind of usability and professional quality I would expect from a brand like Plantronics, and all the while it works well as a stereo headset for music/gaming/etc as well. Very comfortable to wear for long hours, I'd highly recommend it for serious users.
text_fidelity_b: Poly - Voyager Focus 2 UC USB-C Headset (Plantronics) - Bluetooth Dual-Ear (Stereo) Headset with Boom Mic - USB-C PC/Mac Compatible - Active Noise Canceling - Works with Teams, Zoom (Certified) & More

text_fidelity_a:
Sony MDR7506 Professional Large Diaphragm Headphone These are without doubt the best headphones I've ever owned. The sound quality is incredible- rich and full without over-emphasizing any part of the sound spectrum. Bass is amazing and brain scrambling. Mid range is clear and precise and not at all obscured by the lower and upper registers. Highs are crisp and clear.
When I put them on for the first time, the fit was comfortable. They are very good at blocking outside sounds. The first music I found on my IPod that I wanted to hear was Dvorak's 9th Symphony. Wonderful. Instruments were distinct and clear. Horns sounded rich and full. A little Springsteen and the Beatles' Sgt. Pepper confirmed that these phones will handle a broad range of musical styles. Sgt. Pepper was the album that made an audiophile of me back in the 60's when it was released. At that time, I had a cheap portable stereo with a tilt out turntable and fold out speakers. I wore out Sgt Pepper on that thing, and then, a friend happened to have it playing on his parents' high end Marantz receiver and impressive speakers when I stopped by one day. I heard things from that music on his system that I had never heard on my cheap stereo, and I was hooked. These phones at less than a hundred dollars give me everything I heard on that high end system all those years ago. I've seen headphones listing for a hell of a lot more, and I can't imagine that they can sound that much better than these Sony's to justify spending several times more for them. I consider these to be an incredible bargain worth every penny.
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDR7506 Professional Large Diaphragm Headphone

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech MX Vertical Wireless Mouse – Advanced Ergonomic Design Reduces Muscle Strain, Control and Move Content Between 3 Windows and Apple Computers (Bluetooth or USB), Rechargeable, Graphite I haven't had this for very long yet, so I can't comment on longevity, but so far I like it. I take it for granted that there will be some sacrifices when using this type of mouse, I just don't expect to get the same flexibility and usability in terms of various buttons and their placements, so I can't really knock it for being a bit worse in that area than some regular, non-ergonomic options. It works very well and the buttons are easy to click and have a nice "click" to them (unlike cheaper ones). Of course, it takes some time to get used to an upright mouse if you haven't used one before, but after a while it becomes easy/natural.

Regarding the wrist angle, I had some wrist pain and in the past I'd used a cheaper upright ergonomic mouse to help. This is not carpal tunnel, I get joint inflammation on the top side of my wrist, so it may be a bit unusual.
When my old ergonomic mouse broke I decided to try a more expensive one in hopes it will last longer. I can't provide any definitive conclusions on whether this particular aspect of my "treatment" really does anything. My ultimate conclusion is that while treating with other things (e.g. braces, compression, cold or hot), using an alternate device sometimes to change the stress points probably doesn't hurt. Sometimes when going back to use my normal mouse, just putting my hand into position seems to cause some strain, so I think this upright position is helping some. But my experience is that if I use anything for too long, I'll find some joint and/or muscle getting stressed. I'm concerned that this upright mouse position may not be as good for my elbow. So my conclusion is mix it up to spread out the strain rather than hammering on a single weak area, and try to be more careful in the future to start treatment sooner, when I see the early warning signs of strain, before it gets bad.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Vertical Wireless Mouse – Advanced Ergonomic Design Reduces Muscle Strain, Control and Move Content Between 3 Windows and Apple Computers (Bluetooth or USB), Rechargeable, Graphite

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black) I made absolutely sure everything was closed before putting it into water, not that one could have much faith in the mechanisms keeping it closed, as they are easy to accidentally open. I put it in the water gently, and only a foot or so, to film some stingrays and fish; this recording went fine. Later that day, I wanted to photograph a tiny little crab. I took one picture from above the water, and one from below. I noticed this time, when I put the camera underwater, that bubbles started to come out the top. I immediately took it out and noticed the screen starting to fog up with condensation and moisture, the first very bad sign. I double checked everything was still closed, and it was. No part of it had been opened. I put it back in, hoping for the best. After coming back to the sand (never having done more than a few feet underwater), I tried to turn it on to get some video. It would not turn on. I checked again, and nothing appeared to be open. I then dried the exterior and opened it, only to discover there was water on the inside. I immediately removed the SD card, in hopes of salvaging it, but the camera was (is) completely dead.

Two days later, there is corrosion forming on the inside from the water, but at least I salvaged the content on the SD card. The results? Video quality is fine above and below water. Photo quality is a mess. Absolutely the worst pics imaginable.
I am so glad I didn't have to pay for this product; I would have been furious it didn't even last a day in the ocean.

I expected more, since I had previously purchased a "Kodak EasyShare Sport C123 12 MP Waterproof Digital Camera", which has been great! That product never failed after much abuse and takes decent picture and video. I'm not sure what happened here, but buyer beware! Try the EasyShare Sport instead.

I'll post some pictures and, if it lets me, some video too. I hope you all find this helpful!

UPDATE: I can't post video (sorry)
Also, I looked at some other reviews that mentioned water getting in while at the pool or in other non-salinated water. Bear in mind that many electronics can survive water immersion if it is fresh water (as opposed to salt water). Many of these reviewers gave the camera more than one star because it was able to work again, but bear in mind this will NOT hold true it Salt water enters the device. Please consider this.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black)

Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black Bose SoundTouch 10 is an excellent system that enables you to have music, podcasts, and audiobooks available at the press of a button in any room with wifi.

The sleek black design is compatible with almost all decors, and is small enough to hide in a corner.

You can access your content via preset buttons on the top of the device or by using the remote.

Set up was easy at first and then got complicated because my PC was connected to the internet both through wifi and cable. Clearly, the cable was unnecessary, but I didn't know that. You only need one connection. I initially set up the system through my ipad air which was intuitive and only took about 10-15 minutes. The reason I had to contact customer support was I wanted to sync my iTunes library to the Bose SoundTouch. The person I spoke with was patient, knowledgeable, and solved the problem. (And, waiting for tech support only took about a minute.)

I tried the sound qulaity with both classical music and PBS news. The music sounded resonant and rich and had plenty of volume. The speech was clear and easy to understand.

NOTE: Day two. Apparently, my iTunes library is so vast (17,000 items) that it was hard to keep it synched with the Bose system. I could have synched it through Bluetooth, but that meant having to remember to Bluetooth on and off via my desktop, and I use the sound on that all the time; so, it wasn't a viable option. Another idea would be to spend $80 for a NAS drive but that didn't appeal to me, either. I will buy the 3.5mm male to male cable so I can attach my ipod directly to the speaker. It will do the trick, but is not the seamless experience I was hoping for.

I can still listen to radio stations from around the world, i Heart Radio, Pandora, and anything that's downloaded through iTunes on my ipad.

This is a great product if you use it with Bluetooth, or don't have an extensive iTunes library to sync.

I hope to have it as long as I have had my Bose radio, which is more years than I can remember.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black

HUION Keydial Mini Bluetooth Programmable Keypad with Dial 5 Keys Anti-ghosting 18 Customized Keys, Wireless Shortcut Keyboard for Drawing Tablet, PC, MacBook, Surface Pro, Laptops I'm no artist in any way but I do want to try getting into digital art. As a present to myself, I purchased the [[ASIN:B083W88L5H Huion Kamvas 13]] to get started. Huion is known for providing great quality in their products while keeping the prices affordable.

As anyone who has used a drawing tablet can attest, with the tablet taking up the main desk space, it's difficult to access the keyboard for all the shortcut keys that help to make the job easier. One option is to use an under-the-desk keyboard tray, but I really don't like doing that as I tend to kick the tray when I get in and out of my chair. Others purchase more expensive hotkey devices such as this one.

While the HUION Mini KeyDial KD100 does not have fancy led lights or e-ink display on the keys, it does have the basics of what one would need. The keys are laid out like the number pad on a full 101-key keyboard and the dial can be used to adjust anything that needs a kind of analog input (volume, zoom, brush size, etc). The keys are preconfigured for the most common shortcuts but each key can be customized.

The Mini KeyDial came in an oddly plain white box with the name Huion printed on top. It's almost like this is a rebranded white-box device but that really isn't a problem. It simply means that the unboxing experience isn't as satisfying as the drawing tablet itself. Once connected to the Huion drivers, the device feels fully integrated to Huion's ecosystem.

It is managed in the same driver/software that Huion uses for its tablets so that once you'll be able to get up and running customizing the buttons immediately.

Last thing to point out is that the dial on this device can support Microsoft's own RaDial drivers to emulate the dial that Microsoft introduced a few years ago for the Surface Studio, allowing it to interact natively with built-in Windows utilities.
text_fidelity_b: HUION Keydial Mini Bluetooth Programmable Keypad with Dial 5 Keys Anti-ghosting 18 Customized Keys, Wireless Shortcut Keyboard for Drawing Tablet, PC, MacBook, Surface Pro, Laptops
